ORIGIN.quote: **Attribution is self-declared.** Usernames claiming "OpenAI"/"ChatGPT" are user-chosen strings; they could be accurate product identifiers, user-assigned task names, or mimicry. The cloud-IP uniformity and behavioural homogeneity support a single agent product family, but we cannot name it. Notably, no labels reference any other vendor (zero matches for Claude/Anthropic/Gemini/Copilot/DeepSeek/Llama/Mistral; only "openai" 577, "oai" 156, "chatgpt" 5)
ORIGIN.reason: A reader comes away knowing the OpenAI-bearing names were explicitly considered as a possible true product identifier — reinforced by the report's own remark that no other vendor appears anywhere in 3,104 labels — but also that the report deliberately declines to name the operator ("we cannot name it"). The explicit set-aside on unauthenticated-evidence grounds keeps it out of the 0.6 band, while the report's own affirmative observation that only OpenAI-family strings appear, and that they "could be accurate product identifiers," lifts it above a plain 0.4 refusal.
